I reproduced the reviewer's Ca-Ca measurement to the digit on the X2 36-mer: min 1.21, max 15.77, mean 6.41 (ratio 13.0x). I confirmed the three-way pLDDT conflict for KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG: 92.8 (app.js:131), 94.8 (app.js:156), 94.3 (app.js:250). I independently enumerated the cross-table identities and got exactly seven (AF3 #3 to X3; #7 to X2 and B1; #8 to P3; #9 to P4; #10 to P1 and M3), every one with conflicting dG and pLDDT, plus four exact duplicate pairs inside the 25. I verified against Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500 (PMC11168924, fetched) that the confidence head emits pLDDT, PAE and PDE plus pTM/ipTM and no energetic quantity. Three sub-claims need correcting (see corrections). Core conclusion stands unchanged and is fatal. Correction: (1) FACTUALLY WRONG: 'the PAE matrix is symmetric by construction'. The ASCII term at app.js:850 indexes only i (`sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length)`), never j, so PAE(i,j) != PAE(j,i). I computed 936 of 1296 cells asymmetric for a 36-mer. This is also self-contradictory with the reviewer's own ground_truth ('PAE is not symmetric'). Delete the sub-claim; the surviving true statement is that the matrix is |i-j|*0.4 plus a row-constant ASCII offset. (2) OVERSTATED: the curve 'can never enter the High (70-90) bin'. Analytic range is [89.0, 99.0], so 89.0-90.0 IS reachable; across all 25 sequences 77 of 876 residue points (8.8%) fall below 90. Only 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' are unreachable. The sharper true defect is that the legend at index.html:388-391 is purely decorative: the line is a fixed cyan (`borderColor: '#00f2fe'`, app.js:804) and no binning is applied to anything. (3) ARITHMETIC NIT: '1208% bond-length variation' should be 1203% ((15.77-1.21)/1.21); pooled across sequences the spread is wider still (1.04-19.08). (4) git ls-files also returns .gitignore, omitted from the reviewer's list; immaterial.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on INTEG-02: I extracted all 25 affinity strings from app.js and redid every calculation in python3 with R = 1.9872041e-3 kcal/mol/K. Every figure the reviewer states reproduces to the digit: at 298.15 K the stated dG is more negative than the stated Kd permits by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol; the Kd/dG ratio spans 665x to 15,729x; HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (-18.4 | 0.32 nM) gives dG_from_Kd = -12.95 and Kd_from_dG = 3.256e-14 M, a 9,828-fold gap; BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (-19.5 | 0.08 nM) is off by 15,729x with an implied Kd of 5.086e-15 M. My OLS of dG on ln(Kd) returns slope 1.0495, intercept 4.6817, R^2 = 0.99391 - identical to the reviewer's 1.0495 / 4.682 / 0.9939 - and slope/R = 528.1 K = 255.0 C. At 310 K the discrepancy narrows to 3.40-5.18 kcal/mol but never closes. The categorical claim that AlphaFold 3 emits no energetic quantity is confirmed against the Nature paper. This finding is the strongest in the review because it is checkable with a calculator and needs no reading of the rendering code. Correction: The biotin-streptavidin anchor is internally inconsistent, which is unfortunate in a finding about dG/Kd consistency: '~10 fM, dG ~ -18.3 kcal/mol' cannot both hold, since 1e-14 M gives -19.10 kcal/mol at 298.15 K and -18.3 kcal/mol gives 3.9e-14 M (39 fM). Pick one anchor and state it self-consistently (Green's Ka = 2.5e13 M^-1 gives Kd 4e-14 M and dG -18.3 kcal/mol). The conclusion is unaffected and if anything sharpened: -19.5 kcal/mol corresponds to 5.1 fM, i.e. roughly 8-fold tighter than the tightest well-characterised non-covalent protein-ligand complex, and all 25 candidates are claimed at or beyond that regime.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on INTEG-03: Provenance and expressibility are confirmed outright. README.md:98 asserts screening was performed; there is no ADMET code, no descriptor calculation, no result file (git ls-files). I verified every absolute string cited: 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323), 'Off-target Binding: None' (app.js:209), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (app.js:281), 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291), plus 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%' (app.js:375) and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: None' (app.js:343) which the reviewer did not list. I recomputed the physicochemistry: X2/B1 (app.js:153/247) carry 13 K+R and 4 D+E for net ~+9 at pH 7.4 with 30.6% W/F/Y; M4 (app.js:329) is +7 with 28.1% aromatic - the reviewer's numbers are right. I fetched the Mitcheson et al. PNAS 2000 abstract (PMID 11005845 verified): Y652 and F656 sit on S6 and 'face the cavity of the channel', with block by structurally diverse small lipophilic compounds. The README's steric-shielding rationale is indeed unsupported. But the reviewer's stated reason overreaches (see corrections). Correction: Point (3) 'Direction' is domain overreach as written. 'Cationic, aromatic-rich, amphipathic sequences are the canonical hERG-blocker pharmacophore' imports a small-molecule SAR (basic nitrogen + lipophilic aromatic, reaching the inner cavity from the cytosolic side) onto a 30-45mer polycation that cannot physically access Y652/F656 at all. The correct and stronger criticism is a category error, not an inverted direction: the site named in README.md:99 is inaccessible to a peptide of this size, so neither 'steric prevention' nor 'blockade' is assertable, and the genuine peptide liabilities are membrane lysis/haemolysis, immunogenicity (ADA/MHC-II) and protease instability - exactly what the reviewer's own required_fix says, which contradicts their point (3). Rewrite the finding to match the fix. Additionally, the reviewer missed the single fastest tell: all 25 records carry the byte-identical string 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:147 through 395) - one value applied to 25 chemically distinct entities is prima facie proof that no per-compound calculation occurred, and it is checkable in one grep.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on INTEG-07: I re-derived the whole dataset. All four exact duplicate pairs confirmed byte-identical: app.js:173/371 (31-mer, FZD8 CRD vs ZO-1/Occludin), 195/319 (41-mer, a7 nAChR ECD vs TLR4/MD-2), 205/361 (37-mer, TrkB D5 vs EAAT2/GLT-1), 153/247 (36-mer, AChE, differing dG/Kd/pLDDT). 'B' confirmed at position 19 of CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH in app.js:173 and :371 and in the AF3 fasta at app.js:130. The A4 demonstration is the reviewer's best single piece of work and I reproduced it to two decimals: 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' (app.js:381) is 37 characters, the chart plots 37 points labelled H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 ..., and the mean 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT' is exactly 94.08. PAE canvas 540x220 for a square matrix confirmed (index.html:399, aspect 2.45). Three corrections below; I am raising severity because my own analysis shows the data-integrity problem is far broader than four duplicate pairs (see missed_by_reviewer item 2). Correction: (1) FACTUALLY WRONG: 'the 99-residue lead candidate is truncated without notice' by the gridSize cap. renderModalPaeHeatmap is called only from openDrugModal (app.js:651) on drug.sequence; the 99-mer lives in AF3_CANDIDATES and never reaches that code path. The only record actually truncated by the cap at app.js:844 is HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (47 residues, app.js:143), losing 2. Also note the cap makes the theoretical PAE maximum 18.5, so the '0 - 30 A' heading (index.html:397) is unreachable at any length, not just for a 36-mer. (2) IMPRECISE: 'the workflow fails outright for three of the entries'. Of the 25 drug records the copy-FASTA path is invalid for exactly three (X4 app.js:173, A3 app.js:371, A4 app.js:381), but AF3 candidate #6 (app.js:130) carries the same 'B' and has no copy control on that tab at all - the composition differs from what is stated. (3) UNVERIFIED: 'rejected by AlphaFold Server input validation' is plausible but I could not confirm it against DeepMind documentation. State it as 'non-standard; will be rejected or silently coerced by prediction pipelines' rather than as observed server behaviour. (4) FIX INCOMPLETE: the proposed validator must also run over AF3_CANDIDATES[].fasta, and the reviewer does not flag the residue-sphere indexing bug at app.js:744/1005 (see missed item 9).

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on INTEG-08: I installed RDKit 2026.03.5 in a clean venv and re-parsed all eight fields, and independently re-fetched all six PubChem records via PUG-REST. Every CID the reviewer cites is correct with the stated formula and MW: Huperzine A 854026 C15H18N2O 242.32; Curcumin 969516 C21H20O6 368.4 (and the isomeric SMILES they quote matches PubChem byte-for-byte); Ginkgolide B 11973122 C20H24O10 424.4; Ginsenoside Rg1 441923 C42H72O14 801.0; Baicalein 5281605 C15H10O5; Asiatic acid 119034 C30H48O5. My RDKit results: Curcumin (app.js:50) PARSE FAILED; Ginsenoside Rg1 (app.js:20) parses to C38H64O14 vs true C42H72O14; Ginkgolide B (app.js:30) parses to C18H22O8 vs true C20H24O10; app.js:60 and :70 are molecular formulas plus prose, not SMILES, rendered under the label 'SMILES Formulation:' (app.js:477); Rg1, Ginkgolide B and Asiatic acid have 21, 12 and 12 stereocentres respectively, all unassigned. The finding is correct and, on my numbers, worse than stated. Two corrections and one important fix defect below. Correction: (1) WRONG REASON, RIGHT CONCLUSION: Huperzine A (app.js:10) does not 'encode 14 carbons' - it does not parse at all. RDKit returns 'SMILES Parse Error: unclosed ring for input: CC1=CC2C(=C)C3C(=O)NC(=C2CC3(C)N)C' (ring-closure label 1 is opened and never closed) and PubChem PUG-REST returns PUGREST.BadRequest 'Standardization failed'. So three of eight fields are hard syntax failures, not one. Fix the reasoning; the finding gets stronger. (2) UNDERSTATED: Baicalein is not merely 'worth a separate chemistry check'. I submitted the repo string to PubChem and it resolves to CID 14372623 = 6,7,8-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one - a different regioisomer, not baicalein (5,6,7-, CID 5281605). It is definitively the wrong molecule, and should be stated as such. Asiatic acid resolves to CID 296191, the stereochemistry-stripped parent rather than CID 119034, consistent with the reviewer's stereochemistry point. Net tally: 6 of 8 fields defective. (3) FIX IS INSUFFICIENT: the proposed CI gate - 'RDKit MolFromSmiles non-null and formula match against the recorded CID' - would PASS the baicalein error, because the wrong regioisomer has the identical formula C15H10O5. I demonstrated this empirically. The gate must compare InChIKey (or at minimum canonical connectivity SMILES) against the recorded CID, never the molecular formula.

I demonstrated this empirically. The gate must compare InChIKey (or at minimum canonical connectivity SMILES) against the recorded CID, never the molecular formula.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on INTEG-09: My own grep for 'cei|cognitive enhancement' across all four files returns only the data literals (app.js:125-134), the leaderboard cell (app.js:886), the chart dataset label (app.js:1063-1064) and the two index.html render sites (:306 th, :316 'Computational Benchmark'). There is no formula, no input list, no normalisation, no validation set and no citation. The absence-claim holds exactly as stated, and the objection - that 'benchmark' asserts a defined reproducible quantity - is correct and proportionately rated. Correction: 'The values also track the rank order almost perfectly' is slightly wrong and should be replaced by a stronger, exactly true statement. CEI is not monotone in rank: rank 4 (CogTrk-DeNovo-01, CEI 93.8, app.js:128) exceeds rank 3 (CogNrf-KeapDis-03, CEI 92.1, app.js:127). |dG| is monotone in rank either (rank 4 is -14.2, rank 5 is -14.8). The defensible finding is therefore sharper: the leaderboard ranking is not reproducible from ANY column the page displays - it follows neither CEI nor binding energy - so the ordering has no stated derivation at all, not merely an undefined one. Drop the inference that the score was 'written to match a pre-decided ranking'; the inversion undercuts it and it is not needed.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: LEAD FINDING MISSED - AlphaFold 3 cannot design sequences at all, so the platform's central capability claim is impossible in principle, not merely unperformed. README.md:22 says the 25 therapeutics were 'designed via AlphaFold3'; README.md:45 says they fuse warheads with 'AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides'; index.html:290 labels the sequence box 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'; index.html:53 says 'AlphaFold3 Sequence-Driven Drug Discovery'. AF3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w, verified via PMC11168924) is a structure predictor conditioned on a supplied sequence; it has no generative or design head and cannot propose, optimise or score a de novo sequence. Every one of the nine findings treats AF3 as a tool that could have been run but wasn't. None states that even a flawless AF3 run could not have produced these sequences - which is the more fundamental error and should lead the report, above the pLDDT labelling. Sequence design requires an RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN-class pipeline, which the reviewer cites for reporting style but never invokes on this point.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: SECOND LEAD FINDING MISSED - fragment recombination is pervasive, not four duplicate pairs. I enumerated all 8-mers across the 24 peptide records: 169 of 321 distinct 8-mers (53%) appear in two or more candidates, and 16 of the 24 sequences have 100% of their residues inside a motif shared with another candidate. Concretely: X1 (app.js:143, 'TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain') and B3 (app.js:267, 'TrkA Extracellular Ig-like Domain') share a contiguous 28-residue block; X1, P2 and A2 (app.js:143/205/361) share a contiguous 37-residue block spanning targets 'TrkB D5', 'TrkB D5' and 'EAAT2/GLT-1' - the last being a 12-transmembrane solute carrier with no Ig fold whatsoever; X2 (app.js:153, 'AChE catalytic gorge') and M4 (app.js:329, 'autophagosomal membrane LC3-II') share a contiguous 32-residue block; M1 (app.js:299, 'Trem2 Ig domain') and P3 (app.js:215, 'GluN2A NTD') share 25 residues. The pipeline is roughly six fragments recombined and assigned to targets post hoc. This is a broader and more damning integrity signal than the four exact duplicates, it is quantitative and reproducible in ten lines of python, and it is the specific reason I raised INTEG-07 to CRITICAL.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: No pharmacokinetics, no route of administration, no blood-brain-barrier story anywhere. Every record asserts delivery specificity in its targets field - e.g. app.js:145 'CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons & DG SGZ Neural Stem Cells)' - for 26-47mer polycationic peptides conjugated to triterpenoid saponins. Peptides of this size and charge have essentially no oral bioavailability and negligible passive BBB permeability, and no targeting or delivery moiety appears anywhere (no TfR/LRP1 shuttle, no CPP rationale beyond incidental cationicity, no intranasal or intrathecal route, no serum-stability statement). The reviewer mentions BBB penetration once, buried in a remediation bullet under INTEG-03. It warrants its own finding, because it is the load-bearing assumption behind every brain-region claim in the document, and it is unaffected by any labelling fix.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The claimed binding modes are geometrically implausible even as hypotheses, which the review never assesses. app.js:154/158 and README.md:61 assert that a 36-mer 'dual-clamps the AChE gorge entrance (PAS) and catalytic site (CAS)'. The AChE active-site gorge is roughly 20 A deep with a narrow bottleneck; simultaneous CAS+PAS occupancy is achieved by small bivalent ligands (bis-tacrines, donepezil-tacrine hybrids), not by a 36-residue polycation that cannot enter the gorge. The same class of objection applies to the Keap1 Kelch 'decoy' and the a7 nAChR ECD contacts. A structural pharmacology review must say that the residue lists are not merely uncited but sterically incompatible with the stated ligand size - otherwise the remediation ('mark as HYPOTHESIS') licenses hypotheses that are physically impossible.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Mixed and self-contradictory AChE residue numbering, in the very material the review credits as 'largely sound'. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)': Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human - two organisms' numbering inside one string. Separately app.js:12 gives 'Trp279 (PAS)' (Torpedo) for Huperzine A while README.md:32 gives 'PAS (Trp286)' (human) for the same compound. No organism or numbering convention is declared anywhere in the repository. Additionally app.js:12 calls the Trp84/Phe330 contact a 'CAS Salt Bridge' while README.md:32 correctly calls it cation-pi; a salt bridge between two neutral aromatics is chemically impossible. These are uncontroversial, individually checkable domain errors.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The bio-conjugate - the thing every number is nominally about - is never represented in machine-readable form. All 25 are described as warhead + linker + peptide, with named chemistry: '1,2,3-Triazole Linker' (app.js:182), 'Azide Linker' (app.js:298), 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' (app.js:152). But the only structure stored is the peptide FASTA: no SMILES, no conjugation site, no attachment residue, no stoichiometry, no molecular weight for any of the 25. Consequently even the one honest feature the reviewer praises - copy FASTA, run it on AlphaFold Server - would model a chemically different entity from the one the page claims, and every dG, Kd and safety value refers to a molecule whose structure does not exist anywhere in the repository. (Note also that an azide is the reagent in CuAAC click chemistry, not the resulting linker.)

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The uniform hERG string is the single fastest demonstration and the review does not use it. All 25 safety fields carry the byte-identical substring 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:147 through app.js:395). One identical value across 25 chemically distinct entities is direct positive evidence that no per-compound calculation was performed, which is stronger and cheaper to verify than INTEG-03's argument from the absence of tooling. It is one grep, and it survives any objection of the form 'the tool ran elsewhere and only the results were pasted in'.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: A rendering bug that falsifies the 'residue-specific' claim independently of any labelling question. Residue spheres are positioned with curve.getPoint(i / seqLength) (app.js:744 and app.js:1005), but a Catmull-Rom curve through n control points parameterises control point i at approximately i/(n-1), not i/n. Every sphere is therefore displaced from the residue it nominally marks, with the error growing along the chain. So even the sequence-driven decoration does not index the residue it claims to - the 'pLDDT color spectrum' spheres are both coloured by residue letter (app.js:747-749, which the reviewer notes only in the ledger and never elevates to a finding) and positioned off-residue.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Reproducibility and archival hygiene, which the reviewer's own provenance scheme depends on. README.md:4 advertises 'License: Private Research' but git ls-files shows no LICENSE file exists. index.html:15-16 load Three.js r128 and an OrbitControls build from a different release (three@0.128.0 examples) from two separate CDNs with no subresource-integrity hashes, so README.md:119-124's instruction to 'open index.html directly in any web browser' fails offline and the rendering stack is unpinned and unverifiable. There is no version number, no DOI, no changelog and no data dictionary. The proposed provenance field and CI gates cannot be enforced or audited without these. (For completeness: I read styles.css in full; it contains layout only and carries no scientific claim, so no finding is hiding there.)
